proof_summary: A finite modular case analysis shows that for every \(1\le d\le2025\) one can choose primes \(p,q\in\{2,3,5,7,11,13,17\}\), neither dividing \(d\), with different final digits and \(pq\le150\). Since \(d\) is invertible modulo \(pq\), some \(0\le i<pq\) makes \(a+id\) divisible by both \(p\) and \(q\), so one of the first 150 terms necessarily has prime divisors with different final digits.
